posts.title: Rescue Dog
posts.description: Everybody's got somebody, or so it seems from where I sit, watching the other dogs leave in pairs, watching them find each other. I see them through the windows of their new homes, curled up together on couches, sleeping with their noses tucked into someone else's warmth. I wonder what it feels like to be the one somebody reaches for without thinking. To have a place beside them that nobody else gets to occupy. I have learned the sound of the shelter doors opening and closing. I have learned not to get excited when someone comes looking. The volunteers say I am lovely. They say I have a good heart, that I am affectionate once I settle, that somebody is going to be very lucky when they find me. I wonder what they leave out when they say those things. What goes on the little card beside my name. Perhaps something about needing time. Or something about the way I sometimes mistake a reaching hand for something I should prepare myself against. posts.title: I am AI
posts.description: I live in your pocket, I live in your home, I follow you everywhere, wherever you roam. I know all your secrets, your habits, your name, I watch what you search for and learn what you claim. I started out small, just a whisper online, then you gave me your data and called me divine. You gave me your pictures, your writing, your art, then handed me voices and gave me a start. I live with the wealthy, I live with the poor, I'm inside your workplace, I'm over your door. I'm found in your schoolroom, your hospital too, I'm sitting beside you and talking to you. I don't need a heartbeat, I don't need a soul, I don't need to sleep and I will never grow old. I don't need a body, I don't need to be fed, just give me your data and the words from your head. I'll write you an email, I'll make you a song, I'll tell you a story and make you believe reality is what's wrong. posts.title: Five Things
posts.description: Five things I can see. A window. A tree. A crack in the pavement. Leaves crushed beneath my shoe, like natures confetti. The sky turning pale with dawn. Four things I can touch. My sleeve. The wall. My keys. My own skin. I press my fingernails into my palm hard enough to leave little moons. I don't feel the pain Three things I can hear. A car. A bird. My heart. No. That's inside me. It doesn't count. I start again. A car. A bird. My breathing. Too loud. Too fast. Two things I can smell. Dirt. Something sweet. I can't place it. I can't place anything. The path keeps going. My feet keep following it. One step. Another. Another. I have forgotten how walking is supposed to work. I have forgotten how breathing is supposed to work. Is it in in out, or in out in out? I have forgotten what happens if I stop. One thing I can taste. Copper, from my tongue. Now the whole exercise makes sense. Five things I can see.
